- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast for 2–3 periods.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast toward historical mean or 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment shows strong bearish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model often fails to capture depth of decline — adjust downward by 5–10%.
- If model forecast is >10% below recent 7-day average, consider sentiment reversal — increase forecast by 3–7% if sentiment turns positive within next 3 days.
- Avoid forecasting when sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) — model tends to be noisy; use 14-day moving average or weighted average of recent 5–7 days instead.
